cohort: Lambing records of a closely-monitored university sheep flock, including 576 lambings (75 dystocia, 283 uneventful, 218 elective caesarean sections) and 980 lambs, collected between 2009 and 2023.
finding: Dystocia remains an important influential factor for lamb mortality even under best practice conditions, while planned caesarean section is associated with excellent clinical recovery and ewe and lamb survival.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was a significant factor for stillbirth (increased odds following dystocia) and showed a tendency for increased odds of postpartal fever episodes following dystocia.
birth_weight: Not specified as an inclusion/exclusion criterion, but low birth weights were identified as the most influential factor for stillbirth and perinatal mortality.
